name: Trust & safety / abuse detection on UGC platforms
category: Adjacent — non-financial abuse on user-generated content
parent_research_topic: Beava use cases — current and potential applications of beava as a real-time feature server

domain_fit.domain_name: Trust & safety abuse detection on user-generated-content platforms (per-poster post velocity, per-asset report velocity, brigading, reply-flooding, mass reporting, spam bursts, coordinated harassment)
domain_fit.one_line_definition: A trust-and-safety / integrity service decides on every post, reply, vote, follow, DM, livestream chat or report — typically within 50–500 ms — whether to allow, throttle, downrank, queue for human review or auto-action it, based on per-poster / per-asset / per-(reporter, target) / per-room rolling velocity and distribution features.
domain_fit.representative_jobs_to_be_done: 1) Throttle or queue posts when per-poster post velocity / DM velocity / reply velocity crosses a behavioural threshold (spam burst, mass-reply attacks, scraper-style activity) — this is the basic 'X posts in 60s / Y replies to N distinct targets in 10m / Z DMs to N distinct recipients' rule that AutoMod, AutoModerator, Bluesky labelers, and Twitch's chat rate-limits all rely on. 2) Auto-action or downrank assets whose per-asset report velocity / unique reporter count crosses a threshold within a sliding window ('this post got 50 reports from 47 distinct accounts in 5 minutes — quarantine immediately'). 3) Detect coordinated brigading / reply-flood / mass-reporting by maintaining per-(reporter, target), per-(replier, target) and per-room aggregates with n_unique on the actor side; e.g., 'N accounts created in the last 7d all replied to the same target in the last 15 min' or 'N accounts all reported the same post within 5 min, originating from M IPs / fingerprints'. 4) Feed downstream ML risk scorers (per-author trust score, per-room toxicity score, per-asset spam score) with consistent rolling features across the writer path (post submit) and the moderator path (review queue). 5) Power adaptive friction — slow-mode chat, CAPTCHA on post submit, age-verification gates, automatic shadow-ban, label-overlays (Bluesky Ozone), report-queue prioritization — based on continuously updated real-time features rather than static thresholds.
domain_fit.event_shapes: Typical events landing in beava as @bv.event: post_create {ts, author_id, room_id, parent_id?, has_media, hashtags[], mention_ids[], text_hash, lang, client_ip_hash, fp}, reply_create {ts, author_id, parent_post_id, target_author_id, room_id, text_hash}, dm_send {ts, sender_id, recipient_id, has_media, text_hash}, vote {ts, voter_id, target_id, direction}, follow {ts, follower_id, target_id}, report {ts, reporter_id, target_id, target_type (post|user|room|asset), reason_code}, livestream_chat {ts, room_id, sender_id, text_hash}, edit / delete / repost / quote events, account_create {ts, account_id, ip_hash, fp, email_domain, invite_code?}. Volume is dominated by post_create, reply_create, vote, and report. Distinct key dimensions: author_id, target_id (post or user), room_id / subreddit / server_id / channel_id, (reporter_id, target_id) pair, (replier_id, target_author_id) pair, ip_hash, device_fp, account_age_bucket, mention_target_id. Bluesky's Ozone, Discord AutoMod, and Reddit AutoModerator all consume essentially this event shape.
domain_fit.feature_shapes: Heavy use of beava counters + n_unique + velocity + distribution primitives over sliding windows (10s / 1m / 5m / 1h / 24h / 7d). Per-author: count(post, 1m/5m/1h), velocity(post), count(reply, 1m), n_unique(target_author_id, 5m) (reply-target diversity — low diversity flags reply-flood), n_unique(room_id, 1h) (room-hopping), count(dm_send, 1m), n_unique(recipient_id, 1h) (DM spray), distribution(text_hash, 1h) (text repetition — low entropy flags spam), count(mention, 5m). Per-target asset (post / user / room): count(report, 5m/1h), n_unique(reporter_id, 1h) — the canonical mass-report signal — distribution(reason_code, 1h), velocity(view), velocity(reply), n_unique(replier_id, 5m) (reply-flood signal on the receiving side). Per-(reporter_id, target_author_id) pair: count(report, 24h/7d) — pairs with high values flag retaliatory / brigading reporting and feed a 'reporter trust' score. Per-room: count(post, 1m), count(report, 5m), n_unique(reporter_id, 5m), velocity(account_first_post) (sudden influx of new accounts posting in one room = raid signal). Per-IP / per-fp: count(account_create, 1h/24h), n_unique(account_id, 24h) (sockpuppet fanout). Distance primitive optionally drives 'this account first posted from 5 different countries in 24h'.
domain_fit.entity_grain: Composite and high-cardinality. Primary keys are author_id / account_id, target_id (post_id, user_id, asset_id), room_id (subreddit, Discord channel, Twitch chat, Bluesky labeler scope), and ordered pairs (reporter_id, target_id), (reporter_id, target_author_id), (replier_id, target_author_id), (account_id, ip_hash), (room_id, account_age_bucket). Coordinated-attack features additionally need (cluster_id, target_id) where cluster_id is computed off-line from a graph-clustering job and pushed in as a side dimension.
domain_fit.window_semantics_required: Sliding windows dominate (10s, 1m, 5m, 15m, 1h, 24h, 7d). Approximate aggregates (HLL for n_unique reporters / repliers / DM recipients, CMS for top-k offending authors per room, T-Digest for text-entropy distributions) are perfectly acceptable on the high-cardinality axes — mass-reporting decisions are monotonic in the count and 1–3 % HLL error is invisible against the moderator's threshold. Session / activity-burst windows are useful for the 'this account posted 200 times in 5 minutes then went silent' pattern. Tumbling windows show up only for transparency-report aggregation (DSA / OSA reporting templates require quantitative period-based stats).
domain_fit.exactly_once_or_idempotency_needs: At-least-once with idempotent counters keyed on event_id is sufficient. Risk scores and moderation decisions are not money — a duplicate-counted report biases the velocity feature in the safe direction (more likely to action). Strict no-double-count is required only for regulator transparency reports, which are batch-materialized off a Parquet event log, not off live counters.

technical_fit.latency_budget: Two operating points. (a) Inline writer path (post / reply / DM submit): p99 < 50 ms feature-fetch is the usable budget before composing UX degrades; Discord, Twitch, X all keep submit-time velocity checks well under that. (b) Asynchronous moderator queue path (auto-quarantine / human review prioritization): seconds-to-tens-of-seconds is acceptable. Beava's published sub-ms TCP+msgpack get / batch_get fits both budgets with headroom; the read fan-out is more modest than recsys (typically 10–40 features per decision vs hundreds).
technical_fit.feature_freshness_sla: Single-digit seconds end-to-end for the writer path; sub-minute for the report-queue path. Brigading and reply-flood attacks ramp in seconds (Meta's threat reports describe brigading bursts that complete in 5–15 minutes), so stale features defeat detection. Beava's push-on-event model with no broker hop fits this strict tier and is materially fresher than the Kafka -> Flink -> Redis pipeline most in-house stacks ship today. [uncertain]
technical_fit.throughput_profile: Highly platform-dependent. Discord publicly handles ~11M concurrent users with very high per-server message rates (Elixir+Rust stack); Reddit reports tens of thousands of posts/min + millions of votes and reports per day; Bluesky as of 2025 sustains tens of millions of events/day; large in-house deployments at Meta / TikTok handle billions of events/day. For a single mid-sized buyer (forum, marketplace integrity, dating-app safety team, mid-size game studio T&S, healthcare-community moderation), sustained ingest is typically 1k–50k EPS with bursts to 100k–500k EPS during raids; a single beava node at the published ~684k EPS (M4, TCP+msgpack, parallel=16) comfortably covers that. A global platform (X, Reddit, Discord, Roblox) is on a different scale entirely and would need horizontal partitioning that beava v0 does not yet ship. [uncertain]
technical_fit.read_to_write_ratio: Roughly 1:1 to 3:1 reads-per-write on the inline submit path (each post_create / reply / report triggers one write and one batch_get of 10–40 features to score the action). Read-heavier (10:1+) on the moderator-queue and analyst-dashboard side where the same per-target features are re-fetched repeatedly for prioritization, sorting and case review. Overall balanced-to-read-leaning, less extreme than the recsys 100:1 fan-out.
technical_fit.state_size_estimate: Dominated by account_id and target_id cardinality. A medium UGC platform (~10M MAU, ~30M posts/month) sees ~10M live authors × ~50–100 active counter slots × ~32 B per counter slot ≈ 15–30 GB hot author state, plus comparable post-side state (rolling 7d of ~7M posts × ~10 counters), plus (reporter, target) pair state which is the cardinality killer if not capped. Total 30–100 GB live state on a single box — fits in RAM on a modern machine but requires aggressive TTL eviction of cold authors / closed posts. Global platforms (Reddit, Discord, X, Roblox) blow well past a single beava node. [uncertain]
technical_fit.cardinality_pattern: Slowly-growing on account_id / room_id (MAU plus signup rate), explosive on post_id / asset_id (millions of new posts per day on large platforms — TTL is mandatory), explosive on (reporter_id, target_id) pair (most pairs are one-shot, classic long-tail), bounded on reason_code and on top-K offending IPs / fingerprints (CMS appropriate). Coordinated-attack cluster_id is bounded by the upstream graph-clustering job.
technical_fit.typical_state_lifecycle_and_ttl: Mixed TTLs. Hot velocity features on author and target: 10s–24h sliding windows. Per-(reporter, target) pair: 7–30 days for retaliatory-reporter detection. Per-room raid features: 1h–7d. Long-term author trust score: 30–90 days rolling, often longer for habitual offenders. Per-asset report state: lifetime of the asset (until deletion / archival), but typically aged out of beava after 7–30 days and persisted in a warehouse. Most state must be evictable on TTL because post_id cardinality is unbounded.
technical_fit.typical_feature_count_per_decision: 10–40 features per writer-path decision (author velocity + author reputation + room rate + asset history + IP / fingerprint reputation + parent-target history). Fewer than the 20–100+ typical of payments fraud because the action surface is more constrained (allow / queue / friction / block), but still favours the batch_get path beava ships.
technical_fit.durability_requirements: Best-effort to crash-safe. Moderation decisions are derived state — a node losing its 5-minute sliding window during a crash produces a few minutes of degraded recall, not a regulatory or financial breach. DSA / OSA / KOSA transparency reporting obligations operate on a periodic basis off batch-materialized event logs, not off the live counters. Beava's WAL + snapshot story comfortably covers the writer-path durability needs. Note that regulator-driven audit retention (Implementing Regulation 2025/1714 quantitative templates) needs a separate warehouse, not beava.
technical_fit.deployment_topology_fit: Strong fit for single-binary regional / sidecar deployments next to the post-submit service or the moderation API. Discord, Bluesky, and Mastodon-style federated topologies are explicitly per-server / per-relay — exactly the shape beava's single-binary model wants. Multi-region active-active is desired by the largest platforms (X, Reddit, Roblox) but not strictly required for a single-region deployment that can tolerate a few minutes of replication lag. The hard ceilings: beava v0 has no in-process sharding (single tenant beyond ~684k EPS or ~100 GB hot state must hand-shard externally), no native multi-tenancy (a vendor like ActiveFence/Alice or Cinder serving many customers on one box has no isolation primitives), and refuse-on-network-FS forces local-disk WAL planning.

commercial_fit.who_buys: Trust & Safety / Integrity / Community Operations engineering teams at (a) social and UGC platforms (Reddit, Discord, Twitch, Bluesky, Mastodon hosts, X, Pinterest, Snap, Tumblr, Nextdoor), (b) marketplace and gig platforms (Etsy, eBay, Airbnb, Vinted, Depop, Mercari, OfferUp, TaskRabbit), (c) dating apps (Match Group — Tinder/Hinge, Bumble, Grindr, Hily, Feeld), (d) gaming and livestream platforms (Roblox, Epic Games, Activision, Riot, Twitch creators, Whatnot, TikTok Live), (e) education / kids platforms regulated under KOSA-style frameworks (Quizlet, Duolingo, Outschool, Khan Academy community features), (f) healthcare / patient communities (PatientsLikeMe, mental-health forums, telehealth chat surfaces), and (g) T&S-as-a-service vendors who would embed beava (ActiveFence/Alice, Cinder, TrustLab, Resolver, Hive AI, Sift Content Integrity, Sumsub) rather than buy a competitor's managed feature store. The buyer is the T&S Eng / Integrity Platform / Safety Signals team — distinct from the corporate Risk team and from Growth.
commercial_fit.market_size_signal: Content-moderation / T&S tooling is a large and rapidly-growing market: analyst estimates cluster around USD 10–15B in 2025 with 13–15 % CAGR through 2030–2035 (Data Bridge ~USD 12.5B 2025; Research Nester ~USD 13.3B 2025 -> USD 26.1B 2030 at 14.5 %; The Business Research Company ~USD 42B by 2035 at 13 % CAGR; Mordor / Grand View / SkyQuest similar order). Vendor scale signals: ActiveFence/Alice (post Spectrum Labs acquisition) protects 3B+ people across 100+ languages and was valued >USD 500M in 2023; Sift's network processes ~1T events/year across the suite; Hive AI raised $50M+ Series E and serves Reddit, Vimeo, Bumble, Yubo and many marketplaces. Vendor pricing: Hive moderation typically $0.001–$0.01 per inference at volume; ActiveFence and Cinder run six- to seven-figure annual contracts at enterprise scale. Adjacent regulatory spend: EU DSA non-compliance fines up to 6 % of global turnover, UK OSA fines up to 10 % of qualifying worldwide revenue (Ofcom already issued the first >£1M fine in 2025), KOSA-style state-level legislation in CA/UT/NY. [uncertain]
commercial_fit.urgency_drivers: 1) Regulatory cliff edges: EU DSA transparency reporting under Implementing Regulation 2025/1714 — providers must start collecting data per the templates from 1 July 2025 with the first harmonised reports due early 2026; UK Online Safety Act illegal-harms duties effective 17 March 2025 and children's-safety duties effective 25 July 2025, with Ofcom enforcement powers (fines up to 10 % of global revenue, service-blocking) actively in use as of late 2025 (21 investigations, 5 enforcement programmes, first >£1M fine issued); EU Commission guidelines on the protection of minors adopted July 2025; voluntary EU CSAM-detection derogation lapsed April 2026 leaving a legal gap that is forcing platform action. KOSA passed the US Senate in 2024 and has bipartisan momentum into 2026. 2) AI-driven abuse: Sumsub's 2025–2026 Identity Fraud Report cites a 180 % YoY increase in multi-step coordinated attacks; LLM-generated spam and 'AI brigading' break heuristic detectors and force buyers to add behavioural features quickly. 3) Public scrutiny: 2025 NPR / 19th News investigations of Match Group's safety practices and Reddit / Bluesky AI-spam controversies create CEO-level pressure to invest in detection infrastructure. 4) Existing tooling pain: in-house teams running Redis + Lua + Flink for velocity features publicly complain about ops overhead (Reddit Anti-Evil team, Discord Trust & Safety, Bluesky relay operators) and are open to a simpler substrate.
commercial_fit.regulatory_or_audit_constraints: EU DSA (Reg. 2022/2065) with Implementing Regulation 2025/1714 transparency-report templates (quantitative and qualitative, first reports due early 2026) — beava itself doesn't satisfy reporting (that needs a warehouse), but the live counters feed the dashboards platforms must keep current. UK Online Safety Act 2023 — illegal-harms duties (17 March 2025), children's-safety duties (25 July 2025), Ofcom enforcement powers including 10 %-of-revenue fines and service-blocking; risk assessments and proportionate safety measures are mandatory. KOSA (US) and parallel state laws (CA Age-Appropriate Design Code, NY SAFE for Kids, UT Social Media Regulation Act). Australian Online Safety Act (AOSA), Singapore OSA, Brazil Marco Civil amendments. GDPR / CCPA — author_id and IP / fingerprint are personal data, argues for short TTL + aggressive hashing (which beava's in-memory + WAL TTL story actually helps with). SOC 2 Type II is table stakes for any platform-buyer's procurement. CSAM regimes (US 18 USC 2258A NCMEC reporting, EU expected CSAM regulation post-derogation gap, Thorn's Safer integration) — beava is NOT the CSAM-hash-match path (that needs PhotoDNA / PDQ / NeuralHash sidecars) but it is the velocity-feature path that complements those. HIPAA only indirectly (healthcare-community moderation).
commercial_fit.time_to_value_signal: Fast — 1–3 days to a working per-author post-velocity + per-asset report-velocity demo on beava, since the @bv.event + @bv.table primitives map directly to the Discord AutoMod / Reddit AutoModerator / Bluesky Ozone signal shape. A realistic 20–40-feature production pilot at a mid-sized UGC platform is a 2–6 week effort once auth and TLS are added (the v0 gaps below). The 'reply-flood + mass-report + brigading' triple-demo is the obvious one-page README example for this vertical.

competition.incumbents: Generic real-time stack overwhelmingly dominated by Redis (counters + Lua, plus Redis Stack with Bloom / CMS / Top-K modules) — every T&S team interviewed publicly (Reddit Anti-Evil, Discord T&S, Bluesky relay) cites Redis as the default. Aerospike at very high cardinality (Roblox, Sony PlayStation). Flink / Materialize / RisingWave for buyers with a Kafka backbone who want SQL semantics — RisingWave has a published 'Real-time features for account-takeover' blog and the same shape applies to T&S. Tecton / Hopsworks / Chalk / Fennel as managed online feature stores feeding XGBoost / two-tower toxicity / spam models. Custom in-Rust services on top of RocksDB / Sled at Discord-scale. Postgres + materialized views at the small end (Bluesky Ozone uses PostgreSQL for moderation state).
competition.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: End-to-end T&S vendors (the buyer would procure these as black boxes that internally subsume the feature-store layer): ActiveFence / Alice (post-Spectrum-Labs, leading enterprise T&S OS, 3B+ users protected), Cinder ('OS for trust & safety', ex-Meta team, $14M raised), TrustLab (DSA/OSA/AOSA compliance focused, ex-Google/Reddit/ByteDance team), Resolver (security/risk/compliance, 1000+ orgs), Hive AI (Hive Moderation, dashboard + ML models, used by Reddit, Bumble, Vimeo), Sift Content Integrity (part of Digital Trust & Safety suite, 16k+ signals, 1T events/year), Sumsub (identity-fraud + transaction monitoring + new AI-Agent Verification 2025/2026), Two Hat / Microsoft Community Sift (acquired by Microsoft, embedded in Xbox/Azure), Spectrum Labs (now Alice). In-house equivalents at Reddit (Anti-Evil + Safety Signals teams), Discord (Trust & Safety eng), Roblox (Sentinel 2024+, real-time voice moderation, multimodal review), Meta (CIB enforcement program), Bluesky (Ozone + Relay-level abuse mitigation), TikTok (in-house ByteDance stack). Beava would more naturally sit underneath one of these vendors or an in-house equivalent than replace them end-to-end.
competition.beava_differentiator: 1) Single binary, no Kafka / Flink / Redis cluster — fits the per-region / per-relay / per-cluster sidecar topology that Bluesky-AT-Proto, Mastodon-Fediverse and Discord-shard architectures actually use. 2) 50+ aggregation primitives natively cover the velocity / n_unique / distribution / distance features T&S literally lives on, without writing Lua scripts or Flink SQL — directly addresses the Redis+Lua maintenance burden that Reddit Anti-Evil and Discord T&S teams publicly cite. 3) Sub-ms TCP+msgpack get / batch_get matches the inline post-submit / reply-submit latency budget; many platforms today bolt on velocity checks asynchronously because the inline path is too tight, which beava could close. 4) Apache-2.0, no open-core — attractive to T&S-as-a-service vendors (Cinder, TrustLab, Hive) who want to embed it rather than depend on a competitor's managed cloud, and attractive to large in-house teams (Reddit / Bluesky) who do not want vendor lock-in on an integrity-critical control plane. 5) Push-on-event ingestion (HTTP/JSON, framed TCP, msgpack) maps directly to how moderation pipelines already shape events; no broker hop. 6) Distance primitive cleanly expresses impossible-travel-style signals for account-sharing detection on dating apps. 7) Native (reporter, target) pair grain — beava's composite-key tables let you express brigading and retaliatory-reporting features (count, n_unique, distribution on pair) as first-class, which Redis requires hand-rolled hash-of-hash schemes for.
competition.where_beava_loses_today: 1) No TLS, no auth in v0 on :8080 / :8081 / :8090 — disqualifying for any production deployment by a regulated platform; effectively limits beava today to in-VPC / behind-mTLS-proxy deployments. SOC 2 / DSA / OSA audit programs all require authenticated access to integrity infrastructure. 2) No in-process sharding — Reddit-, Discord-, X-, Roblox-scale platforms exceed a single box; the single-tenant ceiling is roughly ~684k EPS and ~100 GB hot state. 3) Refuse-on-network-FS plus in-memory-only means buyers must plan local-disk WAL and bound cold-start replay time; a node restart during an active raid is an outage. 4) No triggers / 'fire when counter crosses threshold' — T&S is inherently event-driven ('fire human-review queue insert when this post's unique-reporter count crosses 25 in 5 minutes'), and today that has to be polled. 5) No multi-tenancy primitives — a T&S-as-a-service vendor serving many customers needs per-tenant namespaces, quotas, and per-tenant rate-limit accounting that beava doesn't ship. 6) No secondary indexes / no 'list all authors with post-velocity > X in last 5 min' query — kills the SOC / analyst surface; T&S analysts at Discord, Reddit, Roblox routinely run this kind of ad-hoc top-K query. 7) No native graph / pair-clustering primitives for coordinated-attack detection (Meta CIB uses URL-sharing-time-similarity graphs, hard to express in pure key-value velocity features). 8) No CSAM / PhotoDNA / PDQ hash-match integration — orthogonal but the buyer expects a story for how it composes with the regulator-mandated hash-match path. 9) No native PII-handling story (IP-hashing at rest, configurable retention windows, right-to-erasure cascading) — GDPR / DSA / KOSA make this load-bearing.
competition.integration_surface: Producers: post-submit / comment-submit / DM-send service (the application server itself, HTTP push), moderation reporting endpoint (one HTTP POST per report), AutoMod-style inline filter (Discord AutoMod, Reddit AutoModerator, Bluesky Ozone labeler, Twitch chat throttle), federation relay (Bluesky Relay, Mastodon Federation), Kafka / Kinesis for platforms with a streaming backbone (Reddit, Twitter/X, TikTok internally). Beava's HTTP/JSON :8080 fits the application-server and webhook producer; TCP+msgpack :8081 fits high-throughput moderation gateways. Consumers: rules engines (AutoModerator YAML rules, Hive auto-rules, Cinder workflow engine, in-house Drools / FEEL), ML scorers (XGBoost spam / toxicity / CSAM-adjacent / grooming-detection models — Hive's pre-trained models, Perspective API for toxicity, in-house transformer rerankers), and inline allow / queue / friction logic in the post-submit RPC.
competition.scoring_engine_coupling: Both. Buyers run deterministic rules (AutoMod / AutoModerator-style YAML or DSL — 'if author_post_velocity_1m > 20 then queue') alongside ML scorers (XGBoost / LightGBM for spam and abuse, transformer-based toxicity models like Perspective and Hive's content moderation suite, ensemble grooming-risk models like Roblox Sentinel). Beava as a pure feature backend stays decoupled from the scorer — both the rules engine and the ML model read from the same batch_get path, which is its natural seam.

adoption_signals.existing_public_users_or_case_studies: No public users of beava on this use case yet. [uncertain] Comparable production systems and published case studies that legitimize the shape of the problem: Reddit Anti-Evil / Safety Signals team job descriptions explicitly call out 'data systems' + 'ML models' + 'user insights' for spam / abuse / bot detection; Discord public engineering blog 'Using Rust to Scale Elixir for 11 Million Concurrent Users' describes the SortedSet primitive used per-guild for messaging (which is exactly the velocity-feature shape); Discord AutoMod public docs describe inline mention-spam and content-spam filters; Bluesky public docs on Ozone (Next.js + PostgreSQL moderation tool, decentralized labelers, AT Protocol stackable moderation March 2024); Roblox Sentinel open-sourced August 2025 for preemptive grooming-risk detection with 256-tick context windows and 35 % of cases caught before user reports (Jan–Jun 2025); Roblox real-time voice moderation achieving 53 % reduction in voice-related abuse reports per DAU; Meta public reports on Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior enforcement (URL-sharing time-similarity graphs as primary signal); Hive AI Moderation Dashboard public docs on user-feed monitoring and auto-moderation rules; Microsoft Community Sift (acquired Two Hat) used in Xbox / Roblox; RisingWave blog 'Real-Time Features for Account Takeover Detection' (analogous shape); Confluent / Conduktor / Kai Waehner blogs on Kafka+Flink fraud-detection patterns that T&S teams adapt.
adoption_signals.community_discussions: No beava-specific Discord / GitHub Discussion threads on T&S use cases located yet. [uncertain] Broader community is very active: Reddit r/RedditEng (engineering blog), Discord engineering blog, Bluesky discussion forums on Ozone + Relay abuse mitigation, Mastodon admin community on per-server moderation tooling, Hacker News threads on Roblox Sentinel (August 2025), DSA / OSA practitioner communities (TrustCon, Marketplace Risk Conference, Integrity Institute).
adoption_signals.examples_or_demos_in_repo: No dedicated T&S / brigading / mass-reporting / reply-flood demo identified in the repository as of the snapshot reviewed. The closest analogues are the generic fraud demo (python/beava/demos/fraud, events.jsonl + schema.json) and the e-commerce demo (python/beava/demos/ecommerce). A natural addition would be examples/trust_safety with post_create / report / reply / dm events keyed on author_id, target_id, (reporter_id, target_id) and room_id. [uncertain]
adoption_signals.adversarial_pressure_level: Maximum. T&S is one of the most actively adversarial domains in tech — attackers retool weekly (LLM-generated spam, residential-proxy sockpuppet networks, coordinated brigading rings, evolving CSAM obfuscation, AI-driven grooming, raid coordination on Telegram / Discord). Feature drift is fast; the buyer expects to add and retire features continuously, which strongly argues for a developer-ergonomic feature backend (beava's @bv.event / @bv.table model) rather than a SQL-on-Flink pipeline that requires a schema-migration to add a new counter. Roblox's 53 %-reduction-in-voice-abuse-reports cited above followed a dedicated infra investment in real-time multimodal review.

risk_and_non_goals.non_goals: 1) CSAM / content hash matching itself — that is PhotoDNA / PDQ / Thorn Safer / NeuralHash territory, not a velocity-counter problem; beava can complement those by counting per-uploader CSAM-hit velocity but cannot replace them. 2) NLP / toxicity / spam classification on raw text — that belongs in Hive / Perspective / in-house transformer models, not beava. 3) Long historical lookback for transparency reports (DSA 1714 quantitative templates require multi-month aggregates) — beava is in-memory; that belongs in Parquet / a lakehouse. 4) Cross-entity graph clustering for coordinated-inauthentic-behavior detection ('which clusters of accounts share IPs and posting times?') — beava has no join engine; that's a graph-DB / OLAP problem, although beava can serve the per-cluster aggregates once a cluster_id is computed externally. 5) Full event archive / forensic case review — WAL is for crash recovery, not analyst-driven case exploration. 6) Acting as the rules engine, the ML scorer, or the moderation UI — beava is the feature backend, not the moderation product. 7) Strict regulator-grade durability for transparency reports — beava could do crash-safe live features but the reporting numbers should be sourced from an auditable warehouse, not from in-memory counters that can age out. 8) Multi-region active-active in v0.
risk_and_non_goals.open_engineering_gaps: Concrete features beava would need to ship to be production-grade for T&S on UGC platforms, roughly in priority order: 1) TLS termination and mutual TLS on :8080 / :8081 / :8090 plus an auth model (token, mTLS, or both) on the push and admin surfaces — without this, no regulated platform (DSA / OSA / KOSA exposure) or T&S-as-a-service vendor can deploy externally; this is the same blocker as bot-defence and is the single most important gap. 2) Triggers / 'fire callback when (target_id).unique_reporter_count crosses 25 in 5 minutes' — T&S is fundamentally event-driven (auto-quarantine, send-to-review-queue, notify SOC, shadow-ban) and polling 10–40 features on every event just to threshold them wastes round-trips; this is the single most-cited workflow gap. 3) HLL / Bloom / CMS / Top-K approximate primitives as first-class aggregations to keep author_id / target_id / (reporter, target) cardinality in bounded RAM during raids; if these are already in the 50+ primitives, document them prominently for this domain with a 'top-K offending authors in last 5 minutes' worked example. 4) In-process or sidecar sharding by key prefix (author_id, room_id, target_id) so platforms beyond ~684k EPS can scale within one cluster without external hand-sharding. 5) Per-key TTL / sliding-window eviction so explosive post_id / report-pair cardinality during raid events doesn't OOM the box. 6) Multi-tenancy: per-tenant namespaces, quotas, and per-tenant rate-limit accounting for vendors serving many customers (ActiveFence, Cinder, TrustLab, Hive). 7) Streaming admin / debug surface and secondary indexes so T&S analysts can run 'top-K authors by post-velocity in last 5 min' or 'top-K targets by unique-reporter count' without materializing the whole keyspace — Discord, Reddit, Roblox internal T&S consoles all expose this view today. 8) Native PII-handling story: IP / fingerprint hashing at rest, configurable per-namespace retention, right-to-erasure that cascades through all derived aggregates (GDPR Art. 17, DSA Art. 14, KOSA-aligned state laws). 9) Composite-key (pair / triple) aggregations as first-class — (reporter, target), (replier, target_author), (room, account_age_bucket) are the natural T&S grains and need to be ergonomic in the @bv.table DSL. 10) Documented hooks for graph-cluster enrichment (external CIB clustering job pushes cluster_id sidecar dimension into beava). 11) Cold-start strategy: WAL replay time on a node with tens of GB of hot author / target state must be benchmarked and bounded; otherwise a restart during a coordinated raid is an outage. 12) CSAM / hash-match integration pattern documented (sidecar to PhotoDNA / PDQ / Safer with beava counting per-uploader CSAM-hit velocity). 13) DSA / OSA / KOSA reference architecture (warehouse for transparency reports + beava for live counters) as a published opinionated pattern.
risk_and_non_goals.trigger_action_required: Yes — strongly. T&S genuinely needs an event-driven trigger primitive ('when target_id.unique_reporters_5m crosses 25, push to review queue'; 'when author_id.post_velocity_1m crosses 30, throttle'; 'when room_id.new_account_post_rate_5m crosses 10x baseline, raise raid flag'). Polling 10–40 features per event to threshold them is workable on the inline writer path because the read is already happening, but is wasteful on the asynchronous quarantine / human-review-queue / SOC-alert path. This is one of the two most-cited gaps for the domain along with TLS + auth.
